title: 342 Petition
statement: A petition the county files to add new claims when a child is already a dependent of the court.
source_says: shall file a subsequent petition
steps: Searched 'WIC 342 subsequent petition', opened the public.law page, read subdivision (a): applies when a minor is already found to be described by section 300 and new facts are alleged.

title: 342 Petition
statement: The court holds a hearing on the new claims, much like the first jurisdiction hearing.
source_says: Unless otherwise provided by law, all procedures and hearings required for an original petition are applicable
steps: Same public.law page, read subdivision (b).

title: 342 Petition
statement: Papers the county files to add new claims to a case that is already open.
source_says: shall file a subsequent petition
steps: Same public.law page, subdivision (a).

title: 366.26 Hearing
statement: The hearing where the court selects a permanent plan for a child when returning home is no longer the goal.
source_says: order termination of reunification services to the parent or legal guardian
steps: Opened public.law WIC 366.22: if child not returned, court orders a 366.26 hearing to decide the permanent plan and ends reunification services. Self-help parents guide also says 'The court must select a permanent plan for your child.'

title: 366.26 Hearing
statement: The judge may terminate parental rights to allow adoption, or establish guardianship or long-term foster care.
source_says: Order that the child remain in foster care
steps: Opened public.law WIC 366.26 and asked for every option in (b) and for the phrase 'long-term foster care'. The phrase does not appear in the section. The options are: end parental rights and adoption, tribal customary adoption, relative guardianship, nonrelative guardianship, permanent placement with a fit and willing relative, or remain in foster care. Adoption and guardianship parts are right. Low harm, wording only.
fix: The judge may end parental rights so the child can be adopted, name a legal guardian, place the child for good with a relative who is fit and willing, or order that the child stay in foster care. For an Indian child, the judge may also order a tribal customary adoption.

title: 366.26 Hearing
statement: The hearing where the judge picks a long-term home for a child who is not going back home.
source_says: The court must select a permanent plan for your child.
steps: Opened the self-help parents guide and the public.law 366.26 page; both describe choosing a permanent plan.

title: 387 Petition
statement: A petition the county files to move a child to a more restrictive placement, for example from a parent's home into foster care, or from a relative's home to a foster home.
source_says: Move your child from a relative's home to a foster care home.
steps: Opened the booklet PDF, glossary entry for 387 petition: 'This happens if CPS believes the child needs a more restrictive placement' plus the two examples. Cross-checked public.law WIC 387(a).

title: 387 Petition
statement: You have the right to a hearing on it.
source_says: shall be made only after noticed hearing upon a supplemental petition
steps: Opened public.law WIC 387, read subdivision (a). Subdivision (d) adds the clerk must set the hearing within 30 days.

title: 387 Petition
statement: Papers the county files to move a child to a different, stricter placement.
source_says: This happens if CPS believes the child needs a more restrictive placement.
steps: Booklet glossary entry for 387 petition.

title: APPLA
statement: Another Planned Permanent Living Arrangement - a permanency plan for older youth when adoption, guardianship, and returning home are not possible.
source_says: If the child is 16 years of age or older, or a nonminor dependent, and no other permanent plan is appropriate
steps: Opened public.law WIC 366.26 and asked for every sentence with 'another planned permanent living arrangement'. Also opened WIC 16501(i)(2), which lists return home, adoption, tribal customary adoption and placement with a fit and willing relative (guardianship is not named there, but 366.26 says 'no other permanent plan').

title: APPLA
statement: Should only be used for youth 16 and older as a last resort.
source_says: for a child 16 years of age or older or a nonminor dependent, when there is a compelling reason or reasons
steps: Opened public.law WIC 16501, read (i)(2). The law's test is a 'compelling reason', and it also covers nonminor dependents.

title: APPLA
statement: A long-term plan for teens 16 and up when they cannot go home, be adopted, or have a guardian.
source_says: the court may order another planned permanent living arrangement
steps: Same 366.26 page as above.

title: Best Interest of the Child
statement: The standard the judge uses for most decisions about a child: what is best for this child's safety, health, and well-being.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: The judge makes these decisions based on what is in your best interests.
steps: Searched for the self-help guide for children and youth, opened it, asked for every 'best interest' passage.

title: Best Interest of the Child
statement: The child's lawyer must tell the judge what the lawyer believes is in the child's best interest, as well as what the child wants.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: In California, your lawyer must tell the judge what is in your best interests and what you want.
steps: Same page. It adds: 'Sometimes those can be two different things.'

title: Best Interest of the Child
statement: What is best for the child. The judge has to think about this.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth
source_says: The judge makes these decisions based on what is in your best interests.
steps: Same page.

title: Biological Parent
statement: A parent by blood, shown by a DNA test or a court judgment.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: A DNA test shows that you are the father of your child
steps: Searched for the self-help parentage guide, opened guide-fathers-other-parents, read the biological father section. Second listed way: 'You have a judgment of paternity from a family law court'.

title: Biological Parent
statement: A biological father who is not yet a presumed parent gets notice of hearings and can try to show he is a presumed parent.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: you have the right to notice of dependency hearings and the right to show that you are a presumed father
steps: Same page, biological father section.

title: Biological Parent
statement: The judge can order services for him if that is best for the child
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: if the social worker and court believe that giving you services would be best for your child
steps: Same page, biological father section.

title: Biological Parent
statement: his relatives are considered for placement.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: Your relatives will also get special consideration when the social worker decides where your child should live.
steps: Same page, biological father section.

title: Biological Parent
statement: A parent by blood, proved by a DNA test or a court.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: You have a judgment of paternity from a family law court
steps: Same page.

title: Bypass
statement: When the court decides NOT to offer reunification services to parents
source_says: Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision
steps: Opened public.law WIC 361.5, read the opening of subdivision (b). The court must find a listed ground by clear and convincing evidence.

title: Bypass
statement: usually due to severe circumstances like aggravated abuse, chronic substance abuse, or previous failure to reunify with a sibling.
source_says: and has resisted prior court-ordered treatment for this problem during a three-year period
steps: Same page, read (b)(6), (b)(10)(A) and (b)(13) in full. Drug or alcohol use alone is not enough: the parent must also have resisted court-ordered treatment in the 3 years before the petition, or failed a case plan treatment program at least twice. The sibling ground also needs a finding that the parent 'has not subsequently made a reasonable effort to treat the problems'.
fix: This can happen only for reasons listed in the law, and the county must prove one with strong proof. Examples: severe physical harm to a child. Or long-term heavy drug or alcohol use when the parent also resisted court-ordered treatment in the last 3 years. Or the parent lost services for a brother or sister and has not made a real effort to fix the problem since.

title: Bypass
statement: This fast-tracks the case to adoption or another permanent plan.
source_says: conduct the hearing pursuant to Section 366.26 within 120 days after the dispositional hearing
steps: Same page, subdivision (f): when services are not ordered the court decides whether to set a 366.26 hearing, and if so holds it within 120 days.

title: Bypass
statement: When the judge decides not to give parents services to get their child back. The case moves faster toward another home.
source_says: Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision
steps: Same page, subdivisions (b) and (f).

title: .26 Hearing
statement: Short for the 366.26 hearing
source_says: On the court papers, it looks like .26 or 366.26, after the number of the law that covers the hearing.
steps: Searched for the booklet, opened the courts.ca.gov PDF, asked for every '.26 / 366.26 / two-six' passage.

title: .26 Hearing
statement: sometimes said "two-six hearing."
source_name: Judicial Council booklet; Self-Help Guide for parents; Caregivers and the Courts; San Bernardino court hearings page; Judicial Council dependency flow chart
source_says: the .26 hearing because the law governing it appears in Welfare and Institutions Code section 366.26
steps: Searched 'two-six hearing 366.26'. Opened five court sources and asked each for 'two-six'. None uses it. They say '.26 hearing' or 'selection and implementation hearing'. Search budget ran out before I could look further. Harmless, but no source.
fix: Short for the 366.26 hearing. Court papers may show it as .26 or 366.26. Some courts call it the selection and implementation hearing.

title: .26 Hearing
statement: It is the hearing where the judge chooses a permanent plan for a child.
source_says: The court must select a permanent plan for your child.
steps: Opened the self-help parents guide and public.law WIC 366.26(b).

title: .26 Hearing
statement: Short for the hearing where the judge picks a permanent plan.
source_says: The court must select a permanent plan for your child.
steps: Same pages as above.

title: 388 Petition
statement: A form (JV-180)
source_says: Request to Change Court Order (JV-180)
steps: Opened the Judicial Council form page for JV-180. It says: 'Fill this out to ask the court to change an order it has made.' Effective January 1, 2020.

title: 388 Petition
statement: that anyone involved in the case can file to ask the court to change a previous order.
source_says: Any parent or other person having an interest in a child who is a dependent child of the juvenile court
steps: Opened public.law WIC 388, read (a)(1). Booklet glossary agrees: 'a paper that you (or other people in your case) can file to ask the judge to change an order'.

title: 388 Petition
statement: For example, a parent might file a 388 petition to ask for more visits, to get services back, or to have the child returned home if circumstances have changed.
source_says: upon grounds of change of circumstance or new evidence, petition the court in the same action
steps: Same page. Note the law also allows 'new evidence', and under (d) the judge sets a hearing only if the change may be in the child's best interests.

title: 388 Petition
statement: A form that asks the judge to change something they already decided.
source_says: Fill this out to ask the court to change an order it has made.
steps: Form page for JV-180.

title: AB 12
statement: The California law that created extended foster care, letting eligible youth stay in foster care until age 21.
source_name: CDSS Extended Foster Care (AB 12) page; WIC 11403(a)
source_says: until age 21
steps: Searched 'cdss extended foster care AB 12', opened the CDSS page: AB 12 created the Extended Foster Care Program and 'became law in 2010'. Also opened public.law WIC 11403(a): 'Nonminor dependents are eligible to receive support until they reach 21 years of age'. WIC 11403 itself does not name AB 12.

title: AB 12
statement: The law that lets you stay in foster care until 21.
source_name: CDSS Extended Foster Care (AB 12) page; WIC 11403(b)
source_says: The nonminor is employed for at least 80 hours per month.
steps: CDSS page and WIC 11403(b): only eligible youth. You need a foster care placement order on your 18th birthday and must meet one of five conditions (finishing high school, college or job school, a job program, working 80 hours a month, or a medical condition). The simple line drops 'eligible'.
fix: The law that lets some youth stay in foster care until 21. You must be in foster care on your 18th birthday. You must also be in school, working at least 80 hours a month, in a job program, or not able to do those because of a health condition.

title: Active Efforts
statement: The extra level of help the county must give a Native American family under the Indian Child Welfare Act.
source_says: is a biological child of a member or citizen of an Indian tribe
steps: Opened public.law WIC 224.1. Active efforts apply 'in any case involving an Indian child'. Under (b) an Indian child is a member or citizen of an Indian tribe, or is eligible and is the biological child of a member. Not every family with Native heritage is covered.
fix: The higher level of help the county must give when the child is an Indian child under the law. That means the child is a member of a tribe, or can become a member and has a birth parent who is a member.

title: Active Efforts
statement: It is more than the reasonable efforts required in other cases.
source_says: in any case involving an Indian child, those efforts and services shall meet the standard of active efforts
steps: Same page, subdivision (f): whenever the county must make reasonable efforts, in an Indian child case those efforts must meet the active efforts standard. The law does not use the words 'more than'; it sets a separate standard that must be met.

title: Active Efforts
statement: The county has to actively work with the family and the tribe to keep the family together.
source_says: shall be conducted in partnership with the Indian child and the Indian child's parents
steps: Same page: 'affirmative, active, thorough, and timely efforts' 'intended primarily to maintain or reunite an Indian child with their family', done in partnership with parents, extended family, Indian custodians and the tribe.

title: Active Efforts
statement: The extra-hard work the county must do to keep a Native American family together.
source_says: A member or citizen of an Indian tribe
steps: Same page. Same issue as the definition: the rule turns on the child being an 'Indian child' under the law, not on Native heritage alone.
fix: The extra-hard work the county must do to keep a family together when the child is a member of a tribe, or can become one through a birth parent who is a member.

title: Adjudication
statement: The court hearing where the judge decides if the allegations in the petition are true.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet p. 9; Self-Help Guide for parents; SLO court glossary
steps: What the hearing does is right: booklet p. 9 says 'the judge will decide whether the allegations in the petition are true' and calls it the jurisdictional hearing. But none of the court sources I opened (booklet, self-help parents guide, Caregivers and the Courts, San Bernardino hearings page, Judicial Council flow chart) uses the word 'adjudication' for it. A general court glossary (SLO) defines adjudication only as 'the rendering of a decision on a matter before a court'. The shared search budget ran out before I could find a California source tying the word to this hearing. No source is listed on the row.
fix: Another word for the jurisdiction hearing. That is the hearing where the judge decides if the allegations in the petition are true.

title: Adjudication
statement: The hearing where the judge decides if what the county said is true.
steps: Same as the definition: the description matches the jurisdiction hearing in the booklet, but I could not find a California court source that calls it adjudication before the search budget ran out.
fix: Another word for the jurisdiction hearing, where the judge decides if what the county said is true.

title: Adoption
statement: A legal process that creates a permanent parent-child relationship between a child and their adoptive parents.
source_says: After adoption, the adopted child and the adoptive parents shall sustain towards each other the legal relationship of parent and child
steps: Searched 'Family Code 8616 legal relationship of parent and child', opened the public.law page, read the whole section. Booklet p. 16 covers 'permanent': 'Once an adoption is final, it cannot be changed'.

title: Adoption
statement: After adoption, the adoptive parents have all the rights and responsibilities of birth parents, and the child legally becomes part of their family forever.
source_says: have all the rights and are subject to all the duties of that relationship
steps: Same public.law page.

title: Adoption
statement: When new parents become a child's legal parents for good.
source_name: Fam. Code 8616; Judicial Council booklet p. 16
source_says: the legal relationship of parent and child
steps: Same page, plus booklet p. 16 on adoption being final.

title: Adoption Assistance Program (AAP)
statement: Financial help for families who adopt a child from foster care who qualifies.
source_name: CDSS Adoption Assistance Program page; WIC 16120
source_says: an entitlement program to provide financial assistance and/or medical coverage to facilitate the adoption of children who otherwise would remain in long-term foster care
steps: Searched 'cdss Adoption Assistance Program', opened the CDSS page. Also opened public.law WIC 16120: 'A child is eligible for Adoption Assistance Program benefits if all of the conditions...'. The cited self-help relatives guide only names AAP in a list and explains nothing.

title: Adoption Assistance Program (AAP)
statement: The amount is set in a written adoption assistance agreement.
source_says: an adoption assistance agreement that stipulates the need for, and the amount of, Adoption Assistance Program benefits
steps: Opened public.law WIC 16120, read (e) and (g). (e) says the family 'has signed an adoption assistance agreement'. CDSS page adds it must be signed before the adoption is final.

title: Adoption Assistance Program (AAP)
statement: It helps make adoption affordable.
source_says: to facilitate the adoption of children who otherwise would remain in long-term foster care
steps: CDSS page. It also says a means test is prohibited.

title: Adoption Assistance Program (AAP)
statement: Money to help families who adopt from foster care.
source_says: provide financial assistance and/or medical coverage to facilitate the adoption of children
steps: CDSS page.

title: Adoption Social Worker
statement: A social worker who steps in when adoption is being considered as the long-term plan.
source_says: An analysis of the likelihood that the child will be adopted if parental rights are terminated.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 366.21, read (i)(1): when a 366.26 hearing is set, the court directs the supervising agency and the county adoption agency (or the state acting as adoption agency) to prepare an assessment. The law says 'adoption agency', not 'adoption social worker'.

title: Adoption Social Worker
statement: This worker looks at whether the child is likely to be adopted and works with the family who may adopt.
source_says: A preliminary assessment of the eligibility and commitment of any identified prospective adoptive parent
steps: Same page, subparagraphs (D) and (G).

title: Adoption Social Worker
statement: The social worker who handles adoption when that is the plan.
source_says: An analysis of the likelihood that the child will be adopted if parental rights are terminated.
steps: Same page.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: The person who becomes a child's legal parent through adoption.
source_says: the adopted child and the adoptive parents shall sustain towards each other the legal relationship of parent and child
steps: Opened public.law Fam. Code 8616.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: Adoption can happen only after the birth parents' rights have ended.
source_says: Order, without termination of parental rights, the plan of tribal customary adoption.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 366.26(b). Option (1) ends parental rights and places the child for adoption. Option (2) is a tribal customary adoption for an Indian child, which does not end parental rights. The booklet (p. 16) only covers the usual case.
fix: In most cases, adoption happens only after the birth parents' rights have ended. One kind is different: a tribal customary adoption for an Indian child does not end the birth parents' rights.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: Once it is final it cannot be undone.
source_says: Once an adoption is final, it cannot be changed no matter what you do.
steps: Opened the booklet, asked for the adoption passages.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: Contact with the birth family afterward happens only if the adoptive parents agree to it in a written post-adoption contact agreement.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet p. 16; Fam. Code 8616.5
source_says: a written agreement to permit continuing contact
steps: Booklet p. 16: 'but only if the people adopting your child agree to what's called a post-adoption contact agreement'. Opened Fam. Code 8616.5 on FindLaw (search result) for 'written'.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: The new legal parent after an adoption. Adoption is permanent.
source_says: Once an adoption is final, it cannot be changed no matter what you do.
steps: Booklet p. 16 and Fam. Code 8616.

title: Allegations
statement: The specific claims of abuse or neglect written in the petition.
source_says: These are called allegations, and they say what the social worker thinks is going on with you and your kids.
steps: Opened the booklet, asked for the definition of allegation and petition (p. 8). No source is listed on the row.

title: Allegations
statement: The things the county says happened.
source_says: These are called allegations, and they say what the social worker thinks is going on with you and your kids.
steps: Same passage.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Someone who may be a child's parent but has not been shown to be one yet.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: you have the right to prove that you are a biological or presumed parent
steps: Opened the self-help parentage guide, alleged parent section.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: You are an alleged parent if the other parent or someone else says you are the parent, or you say so yourself.
source_name: Self-Help Guide for fathers and other parents; WIC 316.2(a)
source_says: if the mother of your child has told the social worker that you are the father or other parent
steps: Same page; second way: 'if you show up to the first hearing and say that you are the parent of the child'. 'Someone else' is backed by public.law WIC 316.2(a): 'the court shall inquire of the mother and any other appropriate person'.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: An alleged parent gets notice of hearings and a chance to prove more.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: As an alleged parent, you have the right to notice of the dependency hearings
steps: Same page. It also says: 'Alleged parents have very few rights in dependency cases.'

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Until then they may not get services, visits, or custody. (services and custody)
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: You might not have the right to custody or reunification services.
steps: Same page, alleged parent section.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Until then they may not get services, visits, or custody. (visits)
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: You might not have the right to custody or reunification services.
steps: Same page. The alleged parent section does not mention visits at all. Only the presumed parent section speaks of 'the right to visitation and custody'. WIC 316.2 does not address visits either.
fix: Until then they might not have the right to custody or to reunification services. Ask your lawyer about visits.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Form JV-505 is how you tell the court.
source_says: Tell the court if you are, or are not, the parent of a child and/or to request testing to determine if you are the parent.
steps: Opened the Judicial Council form page: 'Statement Regarding Parentage (Juvenile)' (JV-505). Note: the text of WIC 316.2 on public.law still calls JV-505 'Paternity-Waiver of Rights', an older title.

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Someone who might be the parent, but it has not been proved yet.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: you have the right to prove that you are a biological or presumed parent
steps: Same page.

title: Appeal
statement: Asking a higher court to review a judge's decision because you believe the judge made a legal mistake.
source_says: An appeal is when someone who loses a case in a trial court asks a higher court (the appellate court)
steps: Opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/appeals: asks the higher court to 'review the trial court's decision'. The part of the page I read did not spell out 'legal mistake'. Fresno court glossary: 'A request to a higher court for review of a lower court ruling.'

title: Appeal
statement: For most orders you have 60 days to file a notice of appeal.
source_says: must be filed within 60 days after the rendition of the judgment or the making of the order being appealed
steps: Opened the courts.ca.gov rule page, read (a)(1). Referee orders run 60 days from when the order becomes final. The rule adds that no court may extend the time.

title: Appeal
statement: Some orders must be challenged by a writ instead, which has a much shorter deadline.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 8.450(e)(4); WIC 366.26(l)
source_says: the notice of intent must be filed within 7 days after the date of the order setting the hearing
steps: Opened rule 8.450: it governs writ petitions on orders setting a 366.26 hearing; 7 days if present, 12 days if told only by mail. Opened public.law WIC 366.26(l)(1): such an order 'is not appealable at any time' unless a timely writ petition was filed. The cited rule 8.406 does not mention writs.

title: Appeal
statement: Asking a higher court to look at the judge's decision.
source_says: review the trial court's decision
steps: Same self-help appeals page.

title: Bailiff
statement: The officer who keeps order in the courtroom.
source_name: Glenn County Superior Court, Who's Who; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.530(b)(10)
source_says: An officer from the sheriff's department who maintains courtroom order and jury custody.
steps: The booklet does not describe the job. Searched court glossaries, opened the Glenn superior court page. Rule 5.530(b) lists 'At the court's discretion, a bailiff' among people entitled to be present.

title: Bailiff
statement: The bailiff wears a sheriff's uniform.
source_says: The bailiff is the person in the sheriff's uniform.
steps: Opened the booklet, asked for the bailiff passage.

title: Bailiff
statement: If you cannot find where to check in when you get to court, ask the bailiff.
source_says: If you can't find the right person to check in with, ask the bailiff.
steps: Same passage.

title: Bailiff
statement: The officer in uniform who keeps the courtroom safe. You can ask them where to go.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet p. 6; Glenn County Superior Court, Who's Who
source_says: If you can't find the right person to check in with, ask the bailiff.
steps: Booklet p. 6. Glenn court page: bailiff provides 'security for the courtroom, the judge, the staff and those in attendance'.

title: Caregiver
statement: The adult your child lives with during the case. A caregiver can be a relative, a close family friend, or a foster parent.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for relatives
source_says: Close family friends and 'non-relative extended family members' may also be entitled to have the child placed in their care.
steps: Opened the self-help relatives guide. It also covers relatives and becoming a 'foster family home (now known as resource family home)'.

title: Caregiver
statement: Caregivers can tell the judge how the child is doing using form JV-290.
source_name: Form JV-290; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(k)(2)
source_says: The child's current caregiver can use this to give written information to the court about the child.
steps: Opened the form page: 'Caregiver Information Form (JV-290)'. Rule 5.534 says the same and also allows a letter. The booklet does not mention JV-290.

title: Caregiver
statement: If you can, build a good relationship with your child's caregiver.
source_says: If possible, keep in touch with your child's caretakers.
steps: Booklet p. 22. Advice, not a rule.

title: Caregiver
statement: The adult a child lives with while the case is open.
source_says: The child's current caregiver
steps: Form page and self-help relatives guide.

title: CASA
statement: Court Appointed Special Advocate.
source_says: CASA is short for Court Appointed Special Advocate.
steps: Booklet glossary.

title: CASA
statement: A trained volunteer the judge assigns
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.655(e)(1), (f)(1); WIC 102
source_says: has been appointed by the juvenile court as a sworn officer of the court
steps: Opened rule 5.655: training 'must include at least 30 hours of formal instruction'. Opened public.law WIC 102: programs 'provide for volunteers to serve as CASAs'.

title: CASA
statement: to one child.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.655; WIC 102
source_says: may be appointed to any dependent, nonminor dependent, or ward
steps: Asked rule 5.655, WIC 102, the booklet and Caregivers and the Courts whether a CASA is assigned to just one child. None says so. Low harm.
fix: A trained volunteer the judge appoints for a child.

title: CASA
statement: A CASA spends time with the child, looks out for what is best for them, and tells the judge how the child is doing.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth; WIC 102
source_says: CASAs are supposed to look out for your best interests and give the court their opinion on how things are going for you.
steps: Opened the self-help children and youth guide. WIC 102: 'Provide independent, factual information to the court'.

title: CASA
statement: A CASA is not a lawyer and not a social worker.
source_says: This person is a volunteer who helps some children in the system.
steps: No source says it in these words. Booklet says a CASA is a volunteer. Rule 5.655(i)(2) bars CASA volunteers from 'Giving legal advice or therapeutic counseling'. Caregivers and the Courts lists the CASA apart from the social worker and the attorney.

title: CASA
statement: Not every county has a CASA program, and not every child gets one.
source_says: Not every county has a CASA program, and there are not always enough volunteers for every child
steps: Booklet glossary.

title: CASA
statement: A trained volunteer who gets to know a child and speaks up for them in court.
source_says: Represent the best interests of the child involved
steps: WIC 102 and the booklet.

title: Case Plan
statement: A written plan listing services and steps parents must complete to have their children returned.
source_says: These are called reunification requirements and are put in your case plan.
steps: Booklet p. 10 and glossary p. 28 ('such as going to a drug treatment program, parenting classes, and counseling'). public.law WIC 16501.1 describes the case plan as a written document. No source is listed on the row. Note the booklet says a case plan can also hold 'dismissal requirements' when the child is at home.

title: Case Plan
statement: The list of things parents need to do to get their child back.
source_says: These are called reunification requirements and are put in your case plan.
steps: Same passages.

title: CFT
statement: Child and Family Team
source_name: WIC 16501(a)(4); CDSS Child and Family Teams page
source_says: a group of individuals who are convened by the placing agency
steps: Opened public.law WIC 16501(a)(4) and the CDSS page ('Child and Family Team (CFT)').

title: CFT
statement: A group that meets to make decisions about a child's care, including family members.
source_says: Providing input into the placement decision made by the placing agency
steps: Same page. The team gives input and recommendations. The placing agency makes the placement decision, and under WIC 16501.1 must 'consider and document the recommendations of the child and family team'. CDSS page speaks of creating a plan together. No source is listed on the row.
fix: A group that meets to plan for a child's care. It includes the child, the family, the caregiver, and helpers. The team gives ideas and advice. The county agency must think about what the team says, but the agency makes the placement decision.

title: CFT
statement: A meeting where family and helpers decide together how to care for a child.
source_says: a convening of all or some members of the child and family team
steps: Same page. The CFT is the team; the meeting is a 'child and family team meeting'. The team gives input, it does not make the final placement decision.
fix: A team of family and helpers who meet to plan how to care for a child. The team gives ideas. The county agency makes the final placement choice.

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: A state list, kept by the California Department of Justice, of people named in substantiated reports of child abuse or severe neglect.
source_says: The Department of Justice shall maintain an index ... all reports of child abuse and severe neglect submitted pursuant to Section 11169
steps: Opened the public.law page for PC 11170 (URL pattern from earlier records) and read subdivision (a). Also opened PC 11169(a): only reports 'determined to be substantiated' are sent. Row cites both sections; they match.

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: Being listed can affect jobs and caring for children.
source_says: concerning any applicant seeking employment or volunteer status with the agency ... responsible for placing children or assessing the possible placement of children
steps: Same PC 11170 page, subdivision (b). The index is shared for hiring, licensing or approval, and child placement checks.

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: The agency that reports you must tell you in writing.
source_says: the agency shall also notify in writing the known or suspected child abuser that he or she has been reported to the Child Abuse Central Index (CACI).
steps: Opened the public.law page for PC 11169 and asked for the exact first sentence of subdivision (c).

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: In most cases you can ask that agency for a hearing to challenge the listing.
source_says: has the right to a hearing before the agency that requested his or her inclusion in the CACI
steps: Same PC 11169 page, subdivision (d). The right is subject to subdivision (e), which the entry covers in its next sentence.

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: A hearing is not available if a court has already found the abuse happened or the matter is still in court.
source_says: shall be denied when a court of competent jurisdiction has determined that suspected child abuse or neglect has occurred, or when the allegation ... is pending before the court.
steps: Same PC 11169 page, exact first sentence of subdivision (e). The same subdivision lets a person ask later if the court case ends with no finding.

title: Child Abuse Central Index (CACI)
statement: A state list of people found to have abused a child. You must be told, and you can usually ask for a hearing.
source_says: determined to be substantiated ... the agency shall also notify in writing ... has the right to a hearing before the agency
steps: Compared the simple line to PC 11169 and 11170. Note for the editor: the finding is made by the investigating agency, not a court, and the list also covers severe neglect. The simple line does not say either, but it does not contradict the statute.

title: Child Abuse Hotline
statement: The county phone line that takes reports about a child who may be unsafe.
source_name: County of San Diego, Child and Family Well-Being, Child Abuse Hotline page
source_says: Report suspected child abuse or neglect at 858-560-2191.
steps: Searched 'San Diego County Child and Family Well-Being Child Abuse Hotline', opened the county hotline page the search returned. This is the source the row cites. It is one county's page; other counties have their own numbers.

title: Child Abuse Hotline
statement: It is open day and night.
source_name: County of San Diego, Child Abuse Hotline page
source_says: You can call 24 hours a day, every day.
steps: Same San Diego County page.

title: Child Abuse Hotline
statement: A parent who is afraid they might hurt their child can also call for help.
source_name: County of San Diego, Child Abuse Hotline page
source_says: A parent afraid you may harm your child
steps: Same San Diego County page. It lists this among the people who should call.

title: Child Abuse Hotline
statement: The phone line to call when a child is not safe.
source_name: County of San Diego, Child Abuse Hotline page
source_says: Concerned about a child's safety
steps: Same San Diego County page.

title: Clear and Convincing Evidence
statement: A higher level of proof than more likely than not.
source_name: Judicial Council of California Civil Jury Instructions, CACI No. 201 (text hosted on Justia)
source_says: Certain facts must be proved by clear and convincing evidence, which is a higher burden of proof.
steps: Searched 'CACI No. 201 Highly Probable clear and convincing proof', opened the Justia copy of the Judicial Council instruction. Its directions say to read it right after CACI 200, 'More Likely True Than Not True'. The row's own source, WIC 361(c), names the standard but does not define it.

title: Clear and Convincing Evidence
statement: The county has to meet it before a judge can remove a child from a parent at the disposition hearing.
source_says: A dependent child shall not be taken from the physical custody of their parents ... unless the juvenile court finds clear and convincing evidence
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 361 and read the opening of subdivision (c). Subdivision (d) uses the same standard for a parent the child was not living with.

title: Clear and Convincing Evidence
statement: Strong proof. More than just "probably."
source_says: the party must persuade you that it is highly probable that the fact is true
steps: Same CACI 201 page.

title: Concurrent Planning
statement: Planning for two goals at the same time - usually reunifying a child with their parents, and at the same time having a backup plan (like adoption by someone else) in case the child can't go home.
source_says: If out-of-home services are used and the goal is reunification ... to be provided concurrently to achieve legal permanency if efforts to reunify fail.
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 16501.1 and read subdivision (g)(10). The statute speaks of 'legal permanency'; adoption is one example.

title: Concurrent Planning
statement: It means the social worker works on both plans so the child doesn't wait too long for a permanent home.
source_says: Services to make and finalize a permanent placement for the child, if efforts to reunify fail, are provided concurrently with services to reunify the family.
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 366.21. Subdivision (l) uses the concurrent services wording. Both sections the row cites support it.

title: Concurrent Planning
statement: Working on two plans at once. Plan A is going home. Plan B is another lasting home, just in case.
source_says: to be provided concurrently to achieve legal permanency if efforts to reunify fail.
steps: Same WIC 16501.1 page.

title: Contested Hearing
statement: A trial. If you disagree with what the county says or recommends and no agreement is reached, the judge holds a contested hearing.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet, Juvenile Dependency Court and You, glossary p. 29
source_says: still cannot agree about what is best for your child after mediation or a settlement conference, there may be a trial, called a contested hearing.
steps: Opened the booklet PDF (URL from earlier records) and asked for the full glossary entry 'Contested hearing'.

title: Contested Hearing
statement: Each side can call witnesses and show evidence, and then the judge decides.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet p. 7; Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.534(g)
source_says: to review evidence and listen to witnesses before deciding what needs to be done
steps: Same booklet, p. 7. Also opened rule 5.534, which lists 'The right to present evidence to the court' and the right to cross-examine witnesses.

title: Contested Hearing
statement: A trial, where each side shows its proof and the judge decides.
source_says: there may be a trial, called a contested hearing.
steps: Same booklet pages.

title: Continuance
statement: When a hearing is moved to a later date.
source_says: This rescheduling is called a continuance
steps: Opened the booklet PDF and read the p. 7 passage on continuances.

title: Continuance
statement: A judge may order one if someone needs more time, a report is late, or a person who must be there is missing.
source_says: Continuances shall be granted only upon a showing of good cause ... Neither a stipulation between counsel nor the convenience of the parties is a good cause.
steps: Opened the booklet (the row's source): the only reason it gives is that the court has too many cases that day. Then opened the public.law page for WIC 352. A delay needs good cause and 'shall not be granted that is contrary to the interest of the minor'. The entry leaves out both limits and its list of reasons is not in the cited source.
fix: A judge can move a hearing only for a good reason, and only if the delay does not hurt the child. Just wanting more time is not enough. Sometimes the court is too busy and the judge picks a new date.

title: Continuance
statement: Ask your lawyer what the new date is and why.
source_says: make sure to write down and remember the new date
steps: Same booklet page. It also says the judge will pick another date and tell you when to come back.

title: Continuance
statement: When the judge moves a hearing to a later day.
source_says: the judge will pick another date and tell you when to come back
steps: Same booklet page.

title: County Counsel
statement: The lawyer for the county social services agency.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.530(d); rule 5.502(29)
source_says: In proceedings brought under section 300, the county counsel or district attorney must appear and represent the petitioner
steps: Opened rule 5.530 on courts.ca.gov and read subdivision (d). Opened rule 5.502: 'Petitioner, in section 300 proceedings, means the county welfare department'. The row's rule citation is right.

title: County Counsel
statement: In court, county counsel speaks for the social worker and argues for what the agency recommends.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.530(d); Judicial Council booklet p. 23
source_says: must appear and represent the petitioner if the parent or guardian is represented by counsel and the juvenile court requests the attorney's presence.
steps: Same rule. The booklet does not use the words 'county counsel'; it says 'the social worker's lawyer' on p. 23.

title: County Counsel
statement: In some counties the district attorney does this job.
source_says: the county counsel or district attorney must appear and represent the petitioner
steps: Same rule. It allows either office. The rule does not say which counties use which.

title: County Counsel
statement: County counsel does not represent you or your child.
source_says: county counsel or district attorney must appear and represent the petitioner
steps: Same rule. County counsel's client is the petitioner, which is the county agency.

title: County Counsel
statement: Your own lawyer is the one who talks with county counsel about your case.
source_says: Tell your lawyer to call the social worker's lawyer
steps: Opened the booklet and read p. 23.

title: County Counsel
statement: The lawyer for the county. Not your lawyer.
source_says: county counsel or district attorney must appear and represent the petitioner
steps: Same rule.

source_says: They must interpret everything that is said. ... Only qualified court interpreters can interpret court proceedings.
steps: Opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/ask-interpreter (URL from earlier records). The booklet the row cites only says to ask the judge for one.

statement: If you do not understand English well, the court gives you an interpreter for free.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, Ask for an interpreter

statement: Tell your lawyer and the judge that you need one.
source_says: you need to let the judge know that you need an interpreter
steps: Opened the booklet, p. 6. It also says to tell your lawyer.

title: Court Interpreter
statement: Someone who puts what is said in court into your language. It is free.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, Ask for an interpreter
source_says: Court Interpreters are provided free of charge.
steps: Same self-help page.

source_says: prepared by CPS describing what is happening with you and your family and what the social worker is recommending the court to order.

source_says: The social worker shall provide the parent or legal guardian, counsel for the child, and any court-appointed child advocate with a copy of the report
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 366.21 and read subdivision (c). That subdivision covers review hearings. The booklet says 'call your lawyer right away so you can see it'.

title: Court Report
statement: Go over it with your lawyer, and tell your lawyer quickly about anything that is wrong.

title: Court Report

source_says: Before each court hearing, you should get a report written by the social worker

title: Chafee Grant
statement: Up to $5,000 a year for college or job training
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant site; CDSS Chafee ETV page
source_says: The California Chafee Grant for Foster Youth (Chafee Grant) awards up to $5,000 a year to eligible foster youth.
steps: Searched 'California Chafee Grant eligibility up to $5,000', opened chafee.csac.ca.gov and the CDSS Chafee ETV page from the results. Both say up to $5,000. Note: the CSAC page also says CDSS 'authorized $4,500 annual award amounts for the 2025-26 academic year', so the real award that year was lower than the cap.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: if you were in foster care at any time between the ages of 16 and 18.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant site
source_says: Be enrolled in an eligible vocational school or college courses at least half-time. ... Payment on an eligible California Chafee Grant Award is not guaranteed. Funding is limited.
steps: Same CSAC page. The foster care rule itself is right: 'a ward of the court, living in foster care, between the ages of 16 and 18'. But the entry reads as if foster care history is enough. The page also requires at least half-time enrollment and satisfactory academic progress, limits the grant to five years, and says payment is not guaranteed.
fix: You may get up to $5,000 a year for college or job training if you were in foster care at any time between ages 16 and 18. You must be in school at least half time. The money is limited, so not everyone who applies gets it.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: It does not have to be paid back.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission Chafee site and FAQ; CDSS Chafee ETV page; San Jose State University financial aid page
steps: Opened chafee.csac.ca.gov, the CSAC Chafee FAQ PDF (April 2023) and the CDSS Chafee page. All call it a grant but none says whether it must be repaid. The FAQ tells schools to 'follow institution policy' if a student's status changes after funds are requested. A San Jose State page (sjsu.edu) says 'You don't have to pay this money back', but that page also shows an old age limit of 22, so I did not rely on it. A further search was blocked because the search limit for this run was used up.
fix: Check with the Student Aid Commission before keeping this line. A safer line until then: It is a grant. Ask your school's financial aid office what happens to the money if you leave school early.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: You must be under 26.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant site; Education Code 69519
source_says: Not have reached their 26th birthday as of July 1st of the award year.
steps: Same CSAC page; the CDSS page says the same. Opened Education Code 69519 on public.law: 'expand program age eligibility of former foster youth up to 26 years of age'. The exact test is the age on July 1 of the award year.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: Money for college or job training for youth who were in foster care between 16 and 18.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant site
source_says: The Chafee Grant may be used at any eligible California college or university, or career or technical school.
steps: Same CSAC page. Eligibility quote: 'a ward of the court, living in foster care, between the ages of 16 and 18'. The row's two sources (Education Code 69519 and the CDSS Chafee ETV page) both exist and are about this program.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: You do not pay it back.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission Chafee site and FAQ; CDSS Chafee ETV page
steps: Same as the definition record. The official CSAC and CDSS pages I opened do not say this. Only a university page does. Search limit reached.
fix: Check with the Student Aid Commission before keeping this line.

title: Child Support Agency

source_says: You have only 30 days to respond to the proposed order

title: Commissioner
statement: A court officer who hears cases in place of a judge.
source_says: The Legislature may provide for the appointment by trial courts of record of officers such as commissioners to perform subordinate judicial duties.
steps: Searched 'California Constitution article VI section 22 commissioners subordinate judicial duties', opened the Justia copy of the section. This is the source the row cites.

title: Commissioner
statement: In dependency court a commissioner may run your hearings and make orders the way a judge would.
source_name: Code of Civil Procedure 259(d); Cal. Rules of Court rules 5.536(b), 5.538(a)(2); WIC 252
source_says: Act as temporary judge when otherwise qualified so to act and when appointed for that purpose, on stipulation of the parties litigant.
steps: Opened CCP 259 on public.law: a commissioner has a judge's power as a temporary judge only 'on stipulation of the parties'. Opened rule 5.536(b): same for a referee. Opened rule 5.538: without that agreement 'The referee must inform the child and parent or guardian of the right to seek review by a juvenile court judge'. WIC 252 gives 10 days. The entry leaves out the agreement and the right to ask a judge for review. Neither rule uses the word commissioner; the booklet does not mention commissioners.
fix: In dependency court a commissioner may run your hearings and make orders. A commissioner has a judge's full power when the people in the case agree to it. If you did not agree, you may be able to ask a judge to look at the decision again. The deadline is short, so ask your lawyer right away.

title: Commissioner
statement: Someone who runs the hearing like a judge does.
source_name: Cal. Const., art. VI, section 22; CCP 259
source_says: officers such as commissioners to perform subordinate judicial duties.
steps: Same sources. As a plain description of the role this matches. See the definition record for the limit it leaves out.

Both list the same limits on staff. These are two trial courts' pages, not a statewide rule. The row's own sources do not say this.

title: Court Reporter
statement: The person who types everything that is said in court.

title: DCFS

source_says: About the Los Angeles County Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS)
steps: Same page. Confirmed for Los Angeles County.

title: De Facto Parent
statement: A person who has been caring for a child on a day-to-day basis and has formed a significant bond with the child.
source_says: a person who has been found by the court to have assumed, on a day-to-day basis, the role of parent, fulfilling both the child's physical and psychological needs
steps: Opened rule 5.502 on courts.ca.gov and read definition (10). The row's number is right. The rule adds that the person must have done this 'for a substantial period' and that the court must make the finding.

title: De Facto Parent
statement: Foster parents or relatives can ask the court to recognize them as de facto parents
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.534(a); form JV-295
source_says: On a sufficient showing, the court may recognize the child's present or previous custodian as a de facto parent
steps: Opened rule 5.534(a). Opened the self-help de facto parent page: the forms are JV-295, De Facto Parent Request, and JV-296, and 'Only the juvenile court judge can decide if you are a de facto parent'.

title: De Facto Parent
statement: which gives them the right to participate more fully in court proceedings.
source_says: grant him or her standing to participate as a party in the dispositional hearing and any hearing thereafter
steps: Same rule. The de facto parent may be present, be represented by a lawyer, and present evidence.

title: De Facto Parent
statement: Source cited: In re Patricia L. (1992)
source_says: a court should liberally grant de facto parent status
steps: Searched 'In re Patricia L. 1992 de facto parent', opened the Justia copy. It is a 1992 California Court of Appeal dependency case about a grandmother's de facto parent status. The citation is real and on point.

title: De Facto Parent
statement: Someone who has cared for a child every day and is close to them. The judge can let them take part in court.
source_says: the court may recognize the child's present or previous custodian as a de facto parent and grant him or her standing to participate as a party
steps: Same rules.

title: Dependency Court
statement: A special court that handles cases where children may need protection from abuse or neglect.
source_says: to provide maximum safety and protection for children who are currently being physically, sexually, or emotionally abused, being neglected, or being exploited
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 300.2, which states the purpose of the dependency law. WIC 325 calls it 'A proceeding in the juvenile court'. The row lists no source.

title: Dependency Court
statement: This is different from criminal court.
source_says: And you need to know this is NOT a criminal court.
steps: Opened the booklet and asked for the p. 20 passage.

title: Dependency Court
statement: The court that decides how to keep kids safe. It is not criminal court.
source_says: This is not criminal court, and the judge is not going to send you to jail.
steps: Same booklet page and WIC 300.2.

title: Dependency Petition
statement: The legal document filed by the county that starts a child welfare court case.
source_says: is commenced by the filing with the court, by the social worker, of a petition
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 325. Opened the JV-100 form page on selfhelp.courts.ca.gov: 'Juvenile Dependency Petition (Version One) (JV-100)', 'The social worker uses this to start a case in juvenile dependency court.' The row's form number is right.

title: Dependency Petition
statement: It describes the allegations of abuse or neglect against the parents under Welfare and Institutions Code Section 300.
source_says: The code section and the subdivision under which the proceedings are instituted. ... A concise statement of facts, separately stated, to support the conclusion
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 332, which lists what the petition must contain.

title: Dependency Petition
statement: The paper the county files to start the case. It says why they think a child is not safe.
source_name: WIC 325; California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: is commenced by the filing with the court, by the social worker, of a petition
steps: Same WIC 325 page. The self-help guide for parents says the petition 'asks the court to open a case to protect your child'.

title: Dependent of the Court
statement: A child the judge has placed under the court's protection after finding that what the petition says is true.
source_says: if the judge decides that any of the allegations are true and your child isn't safe, then your child will become a dependent of the court.
steps: Opened the booklet, p. 9. Also opened WIC 360(d): the court 'may order and adjudge the child to be a dependent child of the court'.

title: Dependent of the Court
statement: It means the court can make orders about the child's care.
source_says: the court may make any and all reasonable orders for the care, supervision, custody, conduct, maintenance, and support of the child
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 362 and read the first sentence of subdivision (a).

title: Dependent of the Court
statement: It does not always mean the child lives away from home.
source_says: Being in the system does not necessarily mean that your child will live with someone else.
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Dependent of the Court
statement: A child the court is watching over to keep safe.
source_says: then your child will become a dependent of the court. That means your child is in the system.
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Detention Hearing
statement: The first court hearing.
source_says: when to go to court for your first hearing. In most courts, this is called the detention hearing.
steps: Opened the booklet, p. 6. The row lists no source.

title: Detention Hearing
statement: The social worker has 2 court days to file papers after a child is removed
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; WIC 313(a)
source_says: The social worker must file the petition within two court days of removing your child.
steps: Opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents. Also opened WIC 313(a): 'within 48 hours after having been taken into custody, excluding nonjudicial days'.

title: Detention Hearing
statement: and this hearing is the next court day.
source_name: WIC 315; California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: This hearing shall be held as soon as possible, but not later than the expiration of the next judicial day after a petition ... has been filed.
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 315. The self-help guide says 'This hearing must be held by the end of the day after the petition is filed.'

title: Detention Hearing
statement: Weekends and holidays do not count.
source_says: within 48 hours after having been taken into custody, excluding nonjudicial days
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 313. The statute's term is 'nonjudicial days'.

title: Detention Hearing
statement: The judge decides if the child should stay in custody.
source_says: to determine whether the child shall be further detained.
steps: Same WIC 315 page.

title: Detention Hearing
statement: The first hearing. The judge decides if the child stays out of the home for now.
source_says: At the detention hearing, the judge will decide whether your child can go home right away.
steps: Same booklet, p. 8.

title: Dismissal
statement: When the judge closes the case. The court and the county agency are no longer involved with your family.
source_says: If the judge dismisses your case, it means that the court and CPS are no longer involved in your life.
steps: Opened the booklet, the source the row cites, and asked for the full glossary entry 'Dismiss'.

title: Dismissal
statement: This usually happens after a child is home and the judge is satisfied the child is safe.
source_says: Once the judge is satisfied that everything is okay, he or she will dismiss your case.
steps: Same booklet, p. 13, in the part about a child living at home. The glossary adds that a case can also be dismissed when a child is placed in a different safe home.

title: Dismissal
statement: When the judge closes the case.
source_says: These are the things you must do before the court will dismiss (close) the case.
steps: Same booklet glossary.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: The hearing where the judge decides what services the parents must complete
source_says: Decide what services you need to make your child safe and able to live with you at home.
steps: Opened the booklet, pp. 9-10, on the dispositional hearing. WIC 358(a) (opened): 'the court shall hear evidence on the question of the proper disposition'.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: and creates the case plan for reunification.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.690(c); Judicial Council booklet p. 24
source_says: Whenever child welfare services are provided, the social worker must prepare a case plan.
steps: Opened rule 5.690 on courts.ca.gov, subdivision (c). The social worker writes the plan and files it by the disposition date; the judge considers it and can order changes. The booklet says the plan 'is adopted at the dispositional hearing'. The judge does not create it. The plan is also not always for reunification, for example when the child stays home.
fix: The social worker writes the case plan. At this hearing the judge looks at the plan and makes it a court order.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: Usually held right after the jurisdiction hearing.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents; Judicial Council booklet p. 9
source_says: Often the jurisdiction and disposition hearings are combined and handled at the same time.
steps: Opened the self-help guide for parents. Booklet p. 9: 'Jurisdiction often happens at the same time as disposition.' WIC 358(a) allows a short delay: up to 10 court days if the child is detained, 30 days if not.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: The court decides where the child will live and what help the family will receive.
source_says: Decide where your child should live (this is called placement).
steps: Same booklet page.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: The hearing where the judge decides where the child lives and what the parents need to do.
source_says: At this next hearing (called the dispositional or dispo hearing), the judge will decide what you should do
steps: Same booklet page. The row's citations, WIC 358 and 361, are both about disposition.

title: DSR
statement: Dependency Status Review. Another name for a review hearing.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: These court hearings are dependency status review (DSR) hearings
steps: Opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents, the source the row cites, and asked for every mention of DSR. The page says the court holds one every 6 months.

title: DSR
statement: Another name for a review hearing.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: These court hearings are dependency status review (DSR) hearings
steps: Same page.

title: Educational Rights Holder
statement: The adult who makes school decisions for a child.
source_says: the adult identified or appointed by the court to make educational or developmental-services decisions for a child, nonminor, or nonminor dependent.
steps: Opened rule 5.502 on courts.ca.gov, definition (13). The row's number is right.

title: Educational Rights Holder
statement: Parents keep this right unless the judge limits it.
source_name: Form JV-535-INFO; Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.650(a)
source_says: can be a parent, guardian, or Indian custodian of the child or youth.
steps: Searched 'JV-535-INFO Information on Educational Rights Holders', opened the form PDF on courts.ca.gov. Rule 5.650(a) (opened) applies 'Whenever it limits, even temporarily, the rights of a parent or guardian'. WIC 361(a)(1) (opened) lets the court limit a parent's control.

title: Educational Rights Holder
statement: If the judge limits a parent's right, the judge names another responsible adult, such as a relative or caregiver, as the educational rights holder.
source_says: the court must determine whether a responsible adult relative, nonrelative extended family member
steps: Opened rule 5.650 on courts.ca.gov. The court uses form JV-535 to appoint. Note: if no responsible adult can be found, the rule has the school district appoint a surrogate or the court make the decisions.

title: Educational Rights Holder
statement: That person can see school records, go to school meetings, and make decisions about things like special education.
source_says: To access records and to authorize the disclosure of information to the same extent as a parent or guardian
steps: Same rule, subdivision (f). It also lists attending the 'individualized education program' and other planning meetings, and consenting to the plan.

title: Educational Rights Holder
statement: The adult who makes school decisions for a child. It is the parent unless the judge picks someone else.
source_says: if the court limits decisionmaking rights and appoints an educational rights holder other than the parent
steps: Same form. Its title is 'Information on Educational Rights Holders', as the row cites.

title: Eighteen-Month Review Hearing
statement: A review hearing held by 18 months after your child was first removed.
source_says: the permanency review hearing shall occur within 18 months after the date the child was originally removed from the physical custody
steps: Opened the public.law page for WIC 366.22, the source the row cites.

title: Eighteen-Month Review Hearing
statement: For most families this is the last chance to have a child returned before the court ends reunification services and moves to a permanent plan.
source_says: Unless the conditions in subdivision (b) are met and the child is not returned ... shall order that a hearing be held pursuant to Section 366.26
steps: Same page. Subdivision (b) lets the court go to 24 months for some parents, and requires six more months of services if reasonable services were not provided. 'For most families' covers those exceptions.

title: Eighteen-Month Review Hearing
statement: The hearing at a year and a half. It is often the last one before a permanent plan.
source_says: shall occur within 18 months after the date the child was originally removed
steps: Same page.
